blindFormulaPacket.note: Blind pass reconstructed from INCI only; claims applied afterwards (Section 3). The 2026-08-26 v1.3 analysis was read as reference only, not reused.
blindFormulaPacket.surfactantArchitecture: Primary: Sodium Laureth Sulfate (2). Co-surfactants after Sodium Chloride (4): Cocamidopropyl Betaine (5), Sodium Cocoyl Glutamate (6, mild amino-acid anionic), Disodium Cocoamphodiacetate (7). Late ether-sulfate blend after the pearlizer: Sodium Laureth-8 Sulfate (9), Magnesium Laureth Sulfate (11), Magnesium Laureth-8 Sulfate (12), Laureth-4 (13), Sodium Oleth Sulfate (14), Magnesium Oleth Sulfate (15) - same alkyl-ether-sulfate family, higher-ethoxylated/Mg salts, typical of a single mild blend raw material.
blindFormulaPacket.conditioningRoutes: No cationic polymer, no silicone, no oil/lipid payload, no protein. Glycol Distearate (10) pearlizer; humectants Urea (3), Panthenol (8).
blindFormulaPacket.scalpActives: None recognized for dandruff (no Piroctone Olamine, no Climbazole). Comfort/humectant routes Urea (3) and Panthenol (8), both before Parfum (16) -> prominent (E3).
blindFormulaPacket.unresolved: Exact concentrations unknown; '3% Urea' is a brand claim (not verifiable from INCI).

cleansingStrength.rationale: Moderate: an early SLES (2) buffered by betaine/amphoteric/glutamate co-surfactants (5-7), no reset intent and no chelator -> C1. The six late ether-sulfate tokens (9, 11-15) are the same SLES family at low level after the pearlizer, not an independent reinforcing reset route.

formulaFacts.ingredient: Sodium Laureth-8 Sulfate / Magnesium Laureth Sulfate / Magnesium Laureth-8 Sulfate / Sodium Oleth Sulfate / Magnesium Oleth Sulfate

counterSignals: Co-surfactants sit after Sodium Chloride (4), so buffering is plausibly modest relative to SLES.
Six ether-sulfate tokens in total; a reader counting tokens would call it strong (the v1.3 analysis did; holdout-v1 lanes split strong/moderate).

conditioningLevel.rationale: Low: cleansing-led formula with no cationic polymer, silicone, fatty-alcohol or lipid deposition; only a pearlizer and two humectants.
counterSignals: Glycol Distearate plus Panthenol/Urea can give a slightly softer feel than a bare cleanser (several light routes).

weightPotential.rationale: Low: no hair-substantive persistent system; the pearlizer and water-soluble humectants rinse off, and the SLES chassis removes residue.
weightPotential.whyThisBand: Deposition absent/light and low-persistence; one light route (pearlizer) can remain low per anchor.
weightPotential.whyNotNeighborBand: Moderate needs one meaningfully persistent system (polymer, silicone, lipid) - none present.
counterSignals: Glycol Distearate can leave a faint film on very fine hair; not persistent.
weightPotential.neighborNote: No plausible adjacent band: zero persistent deposition routes.

careDirection.limitation: Humectants act mainly on scalp feel in a rinse-off; no length-deposition support.

focusPrimary.rationale: scalp_active: the exact-product claim (captured 2026-08-26) positions it for daily cleansing of sensitive scalp with 3% urea and skin-neutral pH, and the formula carries prominent comfort/humectant routes, so scalpComfortTarget is targeted (7.2 row 'explicit sensitive ... scalp positioning with targeted').
focusPrimary.counterSignal: SLES-led chassis and declared Parfum (16) argue against a truly gentle sensitive-scalp product; the exact-GTIN claim exists only as a non-verbatim capture of a page that is now delisted.
focusPrimary.decisionTrace: Blind: urea/panthenol comfort cluster, no hair-care cluster -> provisional scalp_active-or-general. Unblind: name 'Jeden Tag' (mildness/everyday = not a focus) plus sensitive-scalp + 3% urea positioning -> scalp_active, kept at moderate because positioning evidence is non-verbatim; if the sensitive claim were discarded, focus falls to general (no other specialist job).

customerFit.customer: Viola (wavy, FINE strands, HIGH density, medium length, colored + bleached, elastic test snaps, dry scalp without flakes/itch, dry lengths, frizz, tangling, low shine, lost wave shape; this shampoo ~1x/week of ~2 washes/week; Syoss Intense Glaze lamination mask as conditioner, Neqi leave-in mist, Neqi Opulent Oil)
customerFit.keepsSeparateFrom: Product truth above is unchanged by this fit (Section 15).
customerFit.verdictShort: Keep for now is OK (no urgent swap), but it is not an ideal match: it cleans the scalp well and stays light on fine strands, yet gives her bleached, breakage-prone lengths nothing. First confirm which bottle she has.
why: Fits: low weight -> does not flatten fine strands or waves; useful as her weekly 'reset' wash given she layers mask + leave-in + oil (prevents build-up that can drag waves down).
Fits: urea + panthenol give a pleasant, less tight feel on a dry-feeling scalp - nice-to-have in a rinse-off, not essential since she has no flakes or itch.

Does not fit: SLES-led cleanser with practically no conditioning; on bleached, dry lengths that snap, any sulfate foam worked into the lengths adds roughness -> more tangling/frizz right after washing and somewhat faster colour fading.
Engine view: her dry scalp maps to the 'trocken' group (expects gentle cleansing); this product projects to the sensitive group with regular cleansing, so it would not be her top engine pick.
Parfum is declared - minor point for a dry scalp, only relevant if she notices tightness or itch.
watch: Sulfate strength on bleached hair: shampoo the scalp only; let the foam run through the lengths, no rubbing of the lengths; lukewarm water.
Always follow with her conditioner/mask on the lengths (she does - good).
Weight on fine hair: no issue from this shampoo; the weight risk in her routine comes from the mask + oil, which this wash helps to remove.
Snapping lengths are a damage/handling topic (bleaching, heat, brushing wet) - this shampoo neither causes nor fixes it.
If her bottle is the newer 'Ultra Sensitiv' version (0% Parfum, glycerin + guar conditioning, no urea), it is the somewhat gentler and more caring of the two - fine to keep.
callQuestions: Kannst du mir kurz ein Foto der Rückseite schicken - steht da '3% Urea' oder 'Ultra Sensitiv / 0% Parfüm'?
Welches Shampoo nimmst du bei der zweiten Wäsche - und schäumst du nur den Ansatz ein oder auch die Längen?
Wie fühlen sich Kopfhaut und Längen direkt nach dem Waschen an: spannt die Kopfhaut, sind die Längen stumpf oder verknotet? Verblasst deine Farbe schnell?
customerFit.swapDirectionIfNeeded: If the call shows tight scalp, tangling straight after washing or fast fading: a mild, sulfate-reduced shampoo for dry/coloured hair that stays light (low weight) - not a rich 2-in-1 - so fine wavy strands keep their shape. Keep a stronger wash like this one for an occasional build-up reset only if she notices her hair getting limp.
customerFit.language: Cosmetic guidance only; no medical claims.
